draft.title: Christian worship and sacraments
card: Worship is how Christians honour God. Most gather as a community, often on Sunday, the day many Christians link with the resurrection of Jesus.
A church service may include prayer, readings from the Bible, a sermon, and singing. The form differs between denominations, which are the different branches of Christianity.
a rite that Christians understand as a sign of God's grace, which means God's free gift of love. Many churches celebrate sacraments, though the number and the meaning differ between denominations.
Baptism is the rite of welcome into the Christian community, using water. In the Eucharist, Christians share bread and wine in memory of the last meal of Jesus with his disciples.
draft.remember: Christians worship together, and many churches celebrate sacraments such as baptism and the Eucharist.

a.q: Which of these is a sacrament celebrated by many Christian churches?
opts: Baptism, a rite using water to welcome a person
A sermon, in which a minister explains a reading
A hymn, sung by the community during a service
A prayer, said by the community at the start
a.why: Baptism is a sacrament, a rite seen as a sign of God's grace. Sermons, hymns and prayers are common parts of worship, but the card does not name them as sacraments, so they are the tempting wrong choices.
a.clue: Which one is a rite that uses water?

b.q: Sam's church shares bread and wine each Sunday in memory of the last meal of Jesus with his disciples. What is this rite called?
opts: The Eucharist
Baptism
A sermon
A Bible reading
b.why: Sharing bread and wine in memory of the last meal of Jesus is the Eucharist. Baptism is also a sacrament, but it is the rite of welcome using water, so it does not fit this case.
b.clue: Think of the sacrament that uses bread and wine, not water.

a.best: Baptism, a rite using water to welcome a person
